name: Anticipatory Playmaker with Shadowing Support
description:
Overview:
This behavior dynamically switches between an attacking playmaker and a defensive/pressure-support role based solely on relative positions (no explicit communication). It anticipates where to make contact with the ball (a lead point toward the opponent goal), and when not the best attacker it actively shadows the most dangerous opponent or blocks passing lanes. It also has a defensive fallback: if an adversary threatens our goal, it retreats to a cutting/covering position between that adversary and our goal.

Key ideas:
- If the ego agent is clearly closer to the ball than the teammate, take the attacking role: move to a point slightly ahead of the ball toward the opponent goal to strike the ball forward (i.e., nudge it toward goal when contact is made). Use velocity damping to avoid overshooting.
- Otherwise act as a support/defender: shadow the nearest dangerous adversary or move to a blocking point that cuts the passing lane between ball and teammate.
- If any adversary is very close to our goal, ignore other roles and move to a covering point on the line between that adversary and our goal.
- Add a small perpendicular offset/jitter to reduce predictability and prevent getting stuck exactly on lines.

Behavioral pseudo-implementation (uses accessible variables and returns torch.tensor of shape (1,2)):

- Constants:
  - max_force = 1.0
  - attack_lead = 0.9  # how far ahead of the ball toward opponent goal to go when attacking
  - block_offset = 0.6 # distance offset for blocking/pass-cut points
  - defend_distance = 0.8 # distance from goal when covering a threatening adversary
  - role_margin = 0.2 # how much closer we must be than teammate to claim ball

- Computations (vector helpers):
  - vec(a,b) = (b_x-a_x, b_y-a_y)
  - norm(v) = v / (eps + length(v))
  - dist(a,b) = length(vec(a,b))

Pseudo-code:

  ego = ego_agent_position
  teammate = teammate_position
  ball = ball_position
  goal = goal_positions  # this is our goal; opponent goal is approximately mirror on field; for make-ahead choose direction from ball away from our goal: dir_to_opponent_goal = -norm(vec(goal, ball))

  d_ego_ball = dist(ego, ball)
  d_tm_ball = dist(teammate, ball)

  # Defensive override: if any adversary is dangerously close to our goal, cover
  nearest_adv = argmin over adversary_positions of dist(pos, goal)
  if dist(nearest_adv, goal) < (field_threat_threshold ~ 1.5):
    # move to a point on the line from goal toward that adversary at defend_distance
    direction = norm(vec(goal, adversary_positions[nearest_adv]))
    target = (goal_x + direction_x * defend_distance, goal_y + direction_y * defend_distance)
  else:
    if d_ego_ball < d_tm_ball - role_margin:
      # Attacker role: go to a lead point slightly ahead of the ball towards the opponent goal
      # approximate opponent goal direction by pointing away from our goal
      opp_dir = norm((ball_x - goal_x, ball_y - goal_y))
      target = (ball_x + opp_dir_x * attack_lead, ball_y + opp_dir_y * attack_lead)
    else:
      # Support role: shadow/block
      # find nearest adversary to ball (most dangerous matcher) and cut passing lane between ball and teammate
      adv_to_ball = argmin over adversary_positions of dist(pos, ball)
      adv_pos = adversary_positions[adv_to_ball]
      # blocking point: between ball and teammate, closer to the line but offset toward the adversary to cut passes
      midpoint = ((ball_x + teammate_x)/2, (ball_y + teammate_y)/2)
      # vector from midpoint toward adversary so we nudge into the passing lane
      cut_dir = norm(vec(midpoint, adv_pos))
      target = (midpoint_x + cut_dir_x * block_offset, midpoint_y + cut_dir_y * block_offset)

  # Add small perpendicular jitter to avoid predictability
  to_target = vec(ego, target)
  perp = (-to_target[1], to_target[0])
  perp = norm(perp) * 0.05
  desired = to_target + perp

  # Force = proportional to desired direction minus damping from current velocity
  desired_dir = norm(desired)
  damping = 0.5
  vel = ego_agent_velocity
  force = desired_dir * max_force - (damping * torch.tensor([vel_x, vel_y]))
  # clamp force magnitude to max_force
  if length(force) > max_force: force = norm(force) * max_force

  action = torch.tensor([[force_x, force_y]])

Notes and rationale:
- The attacker role aims not to go exactly to the ball center but slightly ahead in the direction of the opponent goal. That increases chances of pushing the ball forward rather than only chasing it.
- The support role is designed to be a passive cutter/shadower: instead of charging the ball, it becomes a utility agent that cuts opponent passing lanes, pressures the nearest dangerous adversary, and positions to receive a pass.
- The defensive override prevents catastrophic mistakes by prioritizing covering threats near our goal.
- All decisions use only observable positions/velocities and distances—no explicit teammate communication is required, but complementary behaviors will naturally coordinate (one agent tends to approach the lead point while the other cuts/pass-cuts).

Tuning:
- attack_lead, block_offset, defend_distance and role_margin can be tuned for aggressive vs conservative play.
- The jitter magnitude and damping control predictability and stability while moving.

This behavior provides a flexible single-agent strategy that alternates between proactive attacking and intelligent support/shadowing to enhance team play without explicit communication.

name: Wide Decoy & Overlap Runner
description:
Overview:
This behavior is a spatial, non-confrontational strategy that deliberately creates and exploits open space rather than always contesting the ball. It acts as a wide decoy to stretch the opponent defense and performs timed overlap runs to receive passes or exploit cutback opportunities. When forced into a defensive situation it becomes a quick interceptor, but its default preference is to avoid direct ball challenges if a teammate is better positioned.

Key ideas (distinct from prior playmaker/shadowing style):
- If the ego agent is clearly farther from the ball than the teammate, do NOT compete head-on. Instead move to a flank position that creates a passing corridor and pulls an adversary out of central lanes.
- If the ego agent is the closest to the ball, become the primary dribbler/charger: approach the ball but bias movement to the side (near sideline) or along a curved cut-in path to keep options open for either a cross or a cutback pass.
- If an opponent is dangerously close to our goal, switch to short-term interception: place yourself between that opponent and our goal at an intercept distance.
- If the teammate appears to be advancing with the ball (teammate velocity directed toward opponent goal), perform a timed overlap: run beyond the teammate into the open flank or behind the defense aligned to the teammate’s motion to be available for a through/cutback pass.
- When neither attacking nor overlapping, maintain a wide lateral offset from the ball to maximize field coverage and force opponents to widen.

Behavioral pseudo-implementation (uses accessible variables and returns torch.tensor of shape (1,2)):

- Constants:
  - max_force = 1.0
  - kp = 1.8  # position stiffness
  - kd = 0.6  # velocity damping
  - side_offset = 1.0  # lateral distance to hold from ball when playing wide
  - close_margin = 0.25  # how much closer to claim the ball
  - defend_threshold = 1.4  # distance to goal considered threatening
  - overlap_speed_threshold = 0.5  # teammate forward speed to trigger overlap
  - cut_in_bias = 0.6  # how much to bias toward cutting in when attacking

- Vector helpers:
  - vec(a,b) = (b_x - a_x, b_y - a_y)
  - length(v) = sqrt(v_x^2 + v_y^2) + 1e-6
  - norm(v) = v / length(v)
  - clamp_mag(v, m) = v * min(1, m / length(v))

Pseudo-code logic:

  ego = ego_agent_position
  vel = ego_agent_velocity
  teammate = teammate_position
  tvel = teammate_velocity
  ball = ball_position
  goal = goal_positions  # our goal

  d_ego_ball = length(vec(ego, ball))
  d_tm_ball = length(vec(teammate, ball))

  # Defensive override: if any adversary is very close to our goal, intercept between them and our goal
  nearest_adv_to_goal = argmin over adversary_positions of length(vec(pos, goal))
  if length(vec(adversary_positions[nearest_adv_to_goal], goal)) < defend_threshold:
    # place on the line from goal to that adversary, but a bit out for interception
    dir_g_to_adv = norm(vec(goal, adversary_positions[nearest_adv_to_goal]))
    target = (goal_x + dir_g_to_adv_x * (defend_threshold * 0.6),
              goal_y + dir_g_to_adv_y * (defend_threshold * 0.6))
  else:
    if d_ego_ball <= d_tm_ball - close_margin:
      # Attacker mode: approach ball but bias to a cutting-in or sideline path
      # Determine approximate opponent goal direction as away from our goal through the ball
      forward_dir = norm(vec(ego, (ball[0] + (ball[0] - goal[0])*0.2, ball[1] + (ball[1] - goal[1])*0.2)))
      # compute lateral perpendicular to forward_dir
      perp = (-forward_dir[1], forward_dir[0])
      # decide side sign based on which side gives more space from nearest adversary
      adv_near_ball = adversary_positions[argmin over adversary_positions of length(vec(pos, ball))]
      side_sign = 1.0 if (dot(vec(ball, adv_near_ball), perp) < 0) else -1.0
      # target is slightly ahead of ball toward goal but offset laterally to run along sideline or cut-in
      target = (ball_x + forward_dir_x * 0.3 + perp_x * side_sign * (-cut_in_bias),
                ball_y + forward_dir_y * 0.3 + perp_y * side_sign * (-cut_in_bias))
    else:
      # Teammate has better access: play wide / decoy or overlap
      # Compute flank point: along line from ball toward opponent goal but offset laterally by side_offset
      approx_opp_dir = norm((ball[0] - goal[0], ball[1] - goal[1]))
      perp = (-approx_opp_dir[1], approx_opp_dir[0])
      # choose flank side that maximizes distance from nearest adversary to that point
      candidate1 = (ball_x + approx_opp_dir_x * 1.0 + perp_x * side_offset,
                    ball_y + approx_opp_dir_y * 1.0 + perp_y * side_offset)
      candidate2 = (ball_x + approx_opp_dir_x * 1.0 - perp_x * side_offset,
                    ball_y + approx_opp_dir_y * 1.0 - perp_y * side_offset)
      d1 = min(length(vec(candidate1, adv)) for adv in adversary_positions)
      d2 = min(length(vec(candidate2, adv)) for adv in adversary_positions)
      flank = candidate1 if d1 > d2 else candidate2

      # Overlap trigger: if teammate is moving forward toward opponent goal, run beyond them
      teammate_forwardness = dot(norm(tvel) if length(tvel)>1e-6 else (0,0), approx_opp_dir)
      if teammate_forwardness > overlap_speed_threshold:
        # run ahead of teammate in the forward direction to offer an overlap
        target = (teammate_x + approx_opp_dir_x * 1.2 + perp_x * (side_offset * 0.5),
                  teammate_y + approx_opp_dir_y * 1.2 + perp_y * (side_offset * 0.5))
      else:
        # default hold the flank to create space
        target = flank

  # Smooth control: PD controller toward target, with damping from current velocity
  pos_err = vec(ego, target)
  desired_force = (kp * pos_err[0] - kd * vel[0], kp * pos_err[1] - kd * vel[1])
  force = clamp_mag(desired_force, max_force)

  # Small random small-phase jitter to avoid purely deterministic runs (keeps formation dynamic)
  jitter = (0.02 * (1.0 if (d_ego_ball > 0.5) else 0.0))
  # apply jitter perpendicular to motion
  f_perp = (-force[1], force[0])
  if length(f_perp) > 1e-6:
    f_perp = norm(f_perp) * jitter
    force = (force[0] + f_perp[0], force[1] + f_perp[1])

  # Return action tensor of shape (1,2)
  action = torch.tensor([[force_x, force_y]])

Rationale and behavioral notes:
- The agent intentionally avoids contest when teammate is better positioned, serving as a "space-creating" wide runner that pulls defenders out of central areas and provides reliable overlap/passing options.
- The attack mode biases movement to the side (cut-in or sideline) instead of directly stabbing at the ball; this yields different offensive shapes (crosses, cutbacks) compared to a direct lead-to-ball attacker.
- Overlap behavior is implicit and based only on teammate velocity direction — no explicit communication required. When the teammate commits forward, the agent times a run beyond them to become a passing target.
- Defensive override ensures immediate risk mitigation if an adversary threatens our goal.
- PD control keeps motion smooth and predictable while the jitter and side-selection logic inject variety to avoid static patterns.

This behavior complements aggressive playmakers by supplying width and timed runs rather than mirroring the same ball-chasing tendencies.

name: High-Tempo Press-and-Break Specialist
description:
Overview:
This behavior specializes in aggressive, high-tempo pressing to regain possession and immediately convert turnovers into fast counters. The agent repeatedly alternates between short burst chases (press) to steal or disrupt an opponent on/near the ball and an explosive forward push (break) that aims to carry or redirect the ball into dangerous space — usually toward a teammate making a forward run or directly toward the opponent goal. If a pressing opportunity is not present or a sudden defensive threat emerges near our goal, the agent quickly reverts to a defensive intercept posture.

Distinctive features (compared to earlier behaviors):
- Emphasis on tempo: alternates short, high-force bursts to force errors, then rapid transitioning into direct counters.
- Predictive press: uses local motion cues (teammate/adversary velocities) to choose which side to approach the ball from to maximize chance of causing a turnover.
- Immediate post-press decision: upon reaching ball-control zone, the agent decides whether to push to teammate (safe counter) or drive toward opponent goal (aggressive break) based on teammate position and nearest adversary.
- Defensive override: strong immediate fallback to cover threats near our goal.

Key ideas and parameters:
- press_range: maximum distance from ball to attempt an aggressive press (short bursts)
- control_radius: distance at which we consider ourselves to be effectively influencing the ball
- burst_force_multiplier: temporary extra force applied during pressing/breaking bursts
- prefer_pass_distance: if teammate is in forward space within this distance, prefer the pass route
- defend_threshold: if an adversary is too close to our goal, abort press and cover
- role_margin: small margin to avoid redundant simultaneous presses with teammate

Vector helpers used below:
- vec(a,b) = (b_x - a_x, b_y - a_y)
- length(v) = sqrt(v_x^2 + v_y^2) + 1e-8
- norm(v) = v / length(v)
- clamp_mag(v, m)
- dot(a,b)

Behavioural pseudo-implementation (uses accessible variables and returns torch.tensor of shape (1,2)):

- Constants:
  - max_force = 1.2
  - burst_force_multiplier = 1.7   # temporary burst when pressing or breaking
  - press_range = 1.2              # only attempt press when within this distance of the ball
  - control_radius = 0.35          # when this close we assume we can influence the ball
  - prefer_pass_distance = 3.0     # distance within which a teammate is a good immediate target
  - defend_threshold = 1.3         # distance to our goal considered dangerous
  - role_margin = 0.15             # avoid contesting teammate when they are clearly closer
  - damping = 0.6                  # simple velocity damping

- Read inputs:
  ego = ego_agent_position
  vel = ego_agent_velocity
  teammate = teammate_position
  tvel = teammate_velocity
  ball = ball_position
  goal = goal_positions  # our own goal
  adv = adversary_positions
  adv_vel = adversary_velocities

- Precompute distances and nearest indices:
  d_ego_ball = length(vec(ego, ball))
  d_tm_ball = length(vec(teammate, ball))
  # nearest adversary to ball (most likely ball holder)
  idx_adv_ball = argmin over adv of length(vec(adv[i], ball))
  adv_near_ball = adv[idx_adv_ball]
  d_adv_ball = length(vec(adv_near_ball, ball))

  # adversary nearest to our goal (defensive override)
  idx_adv_goal = argmin over adv of length(vec(adv[i], goal))
  adv_near_goal = adv[idx_adv_goal]
  d_adv_goal = length(vec(adv_near_goal, goal))

- Defensive override (highest priority):
  if d_adv_goal < defend_threshold:
    # place between that adversary and our goal at a small offset outward
    dir = norm(vec(goal, adv_near_goal))  # from our goal toward adversary
    target = (goal[0] + dir[0] * (defend_threshold * 0.6),
              goal[1] + dir[1] * (defend_threshold * 0.6))
    burst = 1.0  # normal movement, no aggressive burst

  else:
    # Evaluate press eligibility: press when an adversary is closest to the ball AND ego is within press_range
    # and not clearly farther from the ball than teammate
    will_press = (d_adv_ball < d_ego_ball + 0.05) and (d_ego_ball <= d_tm_ball - role_margin or d_ego_ball < press_range)

    if will_press and d_ego_ball <= press_range:
      # PRESS PHASE: approach the ball with a short aggressive vector chosen to maximize disruption.
      # Choose approach side: come from the side opposite the adversary's likely escape direction.
      # approximate adversary's intended escape dir by their velocity; if nearly zero, use vector away from our goal
      adv_motion = adv_vel[idx_adv_ball] if length(adv_vel[idx_adv_ball]) > 1e-6 else vec(goal, ball)
      escape_dir = norm(adv_motion)
      # approach from slightly behind the adversary relative to escape_dir (i.e., intercept from angle)
      approach_dir = -escape_dir  # come opposite to escape
      # if approach_dir is degenerate, just go straight to the ball
      if length(approach_dir) < 1e-6:
        approach_point = ball
      else:
        approach_point = (ball[0] + approach_dir[0] * 0.25, ball[1] + approach_dir[1] * 0.25)

      target = approach_point
      burst = burst_force_multiplier

    elif d_ego_ball <= control_radius or d_ego_ball < d_tm_ball - role_margin:
      # CONTROL/ BREAK PHASE: ego is effectively touching or closest to ball: decide quick counter
      # Determine a direct fast route: prefer a forward push toward teammate if teammate is in better forward space,
      # otherwise drive toward the opponent goal.

      # Approximate opponent goal direction as away from our goal through ball
      opp_dir = norm(vec(goal, ball))
      # Compute teammate forwardness relative to ball (is teammate ahead toward opponent goal?)
      to_teammate = vec(ball, teammate)
      teammate_ahead = dot(norm(to_teammate) if length(to_teammate)>1e-6 else (0,0), -opp_dir) > 0.5
      teammate_close_forward = length(to_teammate) < prefer_pass_distance and teammate_ahead

      if teammate_close_forward:
        # PASS-ORIENTED BREAK: push toward teammate but aim to place ball in front of them, not directly at their feet
        pass_target = (teammate[0] + norm(vec(teammate, (teammate[0] - goal[0], teammate[1] - goal[1])))[0]*0.4,
                       teammate[1] + norm(vec(teammate, (teammate[0] - goal[0], teammate[1] - goal[1])))[1]*0.4) if length(vec(teammate, (teammate[0] - goal[0], teammate[1] - goal[1])))>1e-6 else teammate
        target = pass_target
        burst = burst_force_multiplier
      else:
        # DIRECT BREAK: push the ball toward opponent goal (approx by away from our goal), aiming slightly to avoid nearest defender
        base_break = (ball[0] - goal[0], ball[1] - goal[1])
        base_break = norm(base_break)
        # offset slightly away from nearest adversary to reduce immediate interception
        away_from_adv = norm(vec(adv_near_ball, ball)) if d_adv_ball>1e-6 else (0,0)
        break_dir = norm((base_break[0] + 0.6 * away_from_adv[0], base_break[1] + 0.6 * away_from_adv[1]))
        target = (ball[0] + break_dir[0] * 0.6, ball[1] + break_dir[1] * 0.6)
        burst = burst_force_multiplier

    else:
      # REPOSITION / READY PHASE: No pressing or control opportunity; take an advanced, central ready position to
      # be able to press quickly or receive a turnover. Position slightly forward and to center relative to ball.
      opp_dir = norm(vec(goal, ball))  # direction from our goal to ball (toward opponents)
      perp = (-opp_dir[1], opp_dir[0])
      # bias toward the middle of the pitch by reducing lateral extremes (keeps agent central)
      center_bias = 0.5
      target = (ball[0] + opp_dir[0] * 1.0 + perp[0] * center_bias * -sign(perp[0] if perp[0]!=0 else 1),
                ball[1] + opp_dir[1] * 1.0 + perp[1] * center_bias * -sign(perp[1] if perp[1]!=0 else 1))
      burst = 1.0

- Low-level control / Force computation:
  # PD-like steering toward target with optional burst magnitude
  pos_err = vec(ego, target)
  desired_dir = norm(pos_err) if length(pos_err) > 1e-6 else (0.0, 0.0)
  base_force = (desired_dir[0] * max_force * (burst if burst>1.0 else 1.0),
                desired_dir[1] * max_force * (burst if burst>1.0 else 1.0))
  # subtract damping based on current velocity to stabilize
  force = (base_force[0] - damping * vel[0], base_force[1] - damping * vel[1])
  # clamp magnitude to max_force * burst_force_multiplier
  force = clamp_mag(force, max_force * burst_force_multiplier)

- Minor randomized micro-adjustment to avoid predictability:
  # small perpendicular jitter when in ready or reposition phases (not during critical bursts)
  if burst == 1.0:
    perp = (-force[1], force[0])
    if length(perp) > 1e-6:
      perp = norm(perp) * 0.03
      force = (force[0] + perp[0], force[1] + perp[1])

- Return:
  action = torch.tensor([[force_x, force_y]])

Behavioural rationale and notes:
- Press-and-break exploits short windows: a quick approach from the adversary's likely escape direction is more likely to cause a turnover than a naive head-on chase. Using adversary velocity as a cue creates more effective approach angles.
- The quick post-press decision balances safety (pass to an available teammate ahead) and aggression (drive toward the opponent goal when safe/difficult to pass). The small offset when passing aims to place the ball in the teammate's run, not at their feet.
- Defensive override ensures the agent does not recklessly press when there is imminent danger near our goal.
- Burst force multiplier creates a distinct signature: short high-energy chases and breaks that differ from steady PD-driven movement.
- Role margin avoids redundant simultaneous contest with teammate: if teammate is clearly closer, the agent defaults to ready/reposition rather than contesting.

Tuning suggestions:
- Increase burst_force_multiplier for more aggressive turnovers (but may overshoot control in small maps).
- Lower press_range to make the agent more conservative about risky presses.
- Increase prefer_pass_distance to favor safe counters via teammate when a reliable forward support exists.

This behavior yields a high-energy, turnover-focused single-agent policy that complements more conservative or space-creating teammates by converting disruptions into rapid attacks while still retaining a defensive safety net.

name: Deceptive Dribbler & Shielding Playmaker
description:
Overview:
This behavior focuses on deception, ball protection and timed releases rather than immediate aggressive pressing or pure space creation. The agent actively becomes a mobile "shield" and deceptive dribbler: when it can reach the ball it will prefer to hold and bait opponents with small feints/oscillations, guiding defenders to commit and then exploiting the opened lane either by nudging the ball forward or presenting a safe passing window for the teammate. When not the best candidate to hold the ball it repositions to become a visible passing outlet or decoy that draws attention. It uses only perception of positions/velocities (no explicit communication), and an internal short-lived hold counter to implement timed holds/feints.

Distinctive features (how it differs from previous behaviors):
- Emphasizes intentional "holding" and deception rather than instant attack or wide flank runs.
- Uses a shielding point between the ball and nearest opponent and small lateral feint oscillations to coax opponents out of position.
- Has a timed release logic: it waits for teammate forward availability or opponent overcommit, then executes a short burst to push the ball into space.
- If teammate is better positioned, it becomes a visible, inside passing outlet rather than running wide or pressing aggressively.

High-level modes:
- Shield-Hold: agent approaches the ball and positions itself between ball and nearest adversary, moving with the ball to protect it. While holding, it adds low-amplitude lateral oscillations (feints) to tempt the nearest opponent to commit.
- Release/Burst: triggered when teammate is in a favorable forward position or the nearest adversary retreats/commits—agent makes a short directed burst to nudge the ball into space (toward teammate or opponent goal direction).
- Outlet/Support: if teammate is clearly closer to the ball, the agent positions in front-of-ball-but-off-center to be an easy pass recipient and to draw defenders.
- Defensive fallback: if any adversary is dangerously close to our own goal, abandon holding and move to cover between that adversary and our goal.

Notes on internal memory: the behavior uses an internal small counter (hold_counter) that increments each step while the agent is in a hold-friendly situation (close to the ball and not contested by teammate). It decays if conditions change. This allows brief timed feints without relying on an external clock.

Constants and helpers used in the pseudocode:
- max_force = 1.0
- hold_distance = 0.45        # distance within which we consider ourselves "in contact" to influence/hold the ball
- shield_offset = 0.25        # how far from ball to position toward our intended cover location
- feint_amp = 0.12            # amplitude of lateral feint oscillation while holding
- feint_freq = 2.0            # frequency of feint oscillation (cycles per second-equivalent)
- release_threshold = 3      # internal hold_counter threshold to consider a deliberate release
- hold_counter_decay = 0.9   # multiplicative decay applied when hold conditions are not met
- role_margin = 0.2          # how much closer we need to be than teammate to claim a hold
- cover_distance = 0.8       # defensive fallback distance from goal when covering
- eps = 1e-6

Vector helpers:
- vec(a,b) = (b_x - a_x, b_y - a_y)
- length(v) = sqrt(v_x^2 + v_y^2) + eps
- norm(v) = v / length(v)
- clamp_mag(v, m) = v * min(1.0, m / length(v))
- perp(v) = (-v_y, v_x)

Pseudocode (reactive + small internal state):

internal (persist across steps):
  hold_counter = hold_counter (initialize 0 on reset)
  feint_phase = feint_phase (initialize 0)

Per-step logic:
  ego = ego_agent_position
  vel = ego_agent_velocity
  teammate = teammate_position
  tvel = teammate_velocity
  ball = ball_position
  goal = goal_positions  # our own goal
  advs = adversary_positions
  adv_vels = adversary_velocities

  d_ego_ball = length(vec(ego, ball))
  d_tm_ball = length(vec(teammate, ball))

  # Defensive fallback: if any adversary is dangerously close to our goal, cover
  idx_adv_goal = argmin over advs of length(vec(advs[i], goal))
  if length(vec(advs[idx_adv_goal], goal)) < cover_distance:
    dir = norm(vec(goal, advs[idx_adv_goal]))  # from our goal toward adversary
    target = (goal[0] + dir[0] * (cover_distance * 0.6),
              goal[1] + dir[1] * (cover_distance * 0.6))
    # reset hold intent
    hold_counter = hold_counter * hold_counter_decay
    burst = 1.0

  else:
    # identify nearest adversary to the ball (likely defender/contester)
    idx_adv_ball = argmin over advs of length(vec(advs[i], ball))
    adv_near_ball = advs[idx_adv_ball]
    d_adv_ball = length(vec(adv_near_ball, ball))

    # compute approximate opponent goal direction: away from our goal through ball
    opp_dir_approx = norm(vec(goal, ball))  # points from our goal toward ball/opponent side

    # Decide intent: can we reasonably hold the ball?
    can_hold = (d_ego_ball <= hold_distance) and (d_ego_ball <= d_tm_ball - role_margin)

    if can_hold:
      # Increase hold counter; we are in holding/shielding posture
      hold_counter = hold_counter + 1

      # Determine shield point: a point slightly on the line from ball toward the agent's chosen protect direction
      # Preferred protect direction is toward teammate if teammate is in a forward/favorable position, otherwise away from nearest adversary
      to_teammate = vec(ball, teammate)
      teammate_ahead = dot(norm(to_teammate) if length(to_teammate)>eps else (0,0), opp_dir_approx) > 0.5

      if teammate_ahead:
        protect_dir = norm(to_teammate)  # protect toward teammate to present a pass
      else:
        protect_dir = norm(vec(adv_near_ball, ball)) if length(vec(adv_near_ball, ball))>eps else (-opp_dir_approx[0], -opp_dir_approx[1])

      # target is slightly offset from the ball toward protect_dir to keep the defender behind
      shield_point = (ball[0] + protect_dir[0] * shield_offset, ball[1] + protect_dir[1] * shield_offset)

      # Add a lateral feint oscillation perpendicular to protect_dir. feint_phase increments each step
      feint_phase = feint_phase + feint_freq * 0.1  # small phase advance; step scale is arbitrary but keeps oscillation
      lateral = perp(protect_dir)
      lateral = norm(lateral) if length(lateral) > eps else (0.0, 0.0)
      feint = (lateral[0] * feint_amp * sin(feint_phase), lateral[1] * feint_amp * sin(feint_phase))

      # If nearest adversary is strongly committing toward us (their velocity points toward ball), bias feint away
      adv_motion_dir = norm(adv_vels[idx_adv_ball]) if length(adv_vels[idx_adv_ball])>eps else (0.0, 0.0)
      adv_committing = dot(adv_motion_dir, norm(vec(adv_near_ball, ball))) > 0.6
      if adv_committing:
        # increase feint amplitude and bias slightly opposite to commitment to draw them
        feint = (feint[0] * 1.6 - adv_motion_dir[0] * 0.05, feint[1] * 1.6 - adv_motion_dir[1] * 0.05)

      target = (shield_point[0] + feint[0], shield_point[1] + feint[1])

      # Decide whether to release now: release if teammate is well-placed ahead or if opponent retreats
      teammate_ready = (length(to_teammate) < 2.5) and teammate_ahead
      adv_retreating = dot(adv_motion_dir, norm(vec(adv_near_ball, ball))) < -0.2 if length(adv_vels[idx_adv_ball])>eps else False

      if (hold_counter >= release_threshold and (teammate_ready or adv_retreating)):
        # RELEASE/BURST: nudge ball toward teammate if safe, else toward opponent goal (away from our goal)
        if teammate_ready:
          # place the ball slightly ahead of teammate along their forward direction
          tm_forward = norm(vec(teammate, (teammate[0] - goal[0], teammate[1] - goal[1]))) if length(vec(teammate, (teammate[0] - goal[0], teammate[1] - goal[1])))>eps else opp_dir_approx
          release_target = (teammate[0] + tm_forward[0] * 0.4, teammate[1] + tm_forward[1] * 0.4)
        else:
          release_dir = norm((ball[0] - goal[0], ball[1] - goal[1]))
          # bias away from nearest adversary slightly to avoid immediate interception
          away_from_adv = norm(vec(adv_near_ball, ball)) if length(vec(adv_near_ball, ball))>eps else (0.0, 0.0)
          release_dir = norm((release_dir[0] + 0.6 * away_from_adv[0], release_dir[1] + 0.6 * away_from_adv[1]))
          release_target = (ball[0] + release_dir[0] * 0.6, ball[1] + release_dir[1] * 0.6)

        # short burst toward release_target
        burst = 1.4
        desired_dir = norm(vec(ego, release_target))
        base_force = (desired_dir[0] * max_force * burst - 0.6 * vel[0], desired_dir[1] * max_force * burst - 0.6 * vel[1])
        force = clamp_mag(base_force, max_force * burst)

        # after release reduce hold intent
        hold_counter = hold_counter * 0.2
        action = 'burst'  # conceptual label; actual returned tensor below
      else:
        # Normal holding motion: move smoothly toward target while damping current velocity
        kp = 1.6
        kd = 0.7
        pos_err = vec(ego, target)
        desired = (kp * pos_err[0] - kd * vel[0], kp * pos_err[1] - kd * vel[1])
        force = clamp_mag(desired, max_force)
        action = 'hold'

    else:
      # We are not in a holdable position. Either teammate is closer (be an outlet) or reposition to request pass.
      hold_counter = hold_counter * hold_counter_decay

      if d_tm_ball <= d_ego_ball - role_margin:
        # TEammate has the ball: become an inside outlet between ball and goal, offset a bit toward center to draw defenders
        ahead_point = (ball[0] + opp_dir_approx[0] * 0.9, ball[1] + opp_dir_approx[1] * 0.9)
        # bias slightly toward pitch center by removing extreme lateral component
        center_bias = 0.5
        target = (ahead_point[0] - opp_dir_approx[1] * center_bias, ahead_point[1] + opp_dir_approx[0] * center_bias)
      else:
        # Neutral reposition: take a short advanced/supporting position near ball but not contesting
        target = (ball[0] + opp_dir_approx[0] * 1.0 + perp(opp_dir_approx)[0] * 0.4,
                  ball[1] + opp_dir_approx[1] * 1.0 + perp(opp_dir_approx)[1] * 0.4)

      # Smooth PD control toward target
      kp2 = 1.2
      kd2 = 0.6
      pos_err = vec(ego, target)
      desired = (kp2 * pos_err[0] - kd2 * vel[0], kp2 * pos_err[1] - kd2 * vel[1])
      force = clamp_mag(desired, max_force)

  # Ensure force tensor output
  # if 'burst' branch already set force, otherwise force computed above
  # final clamp and return as torch.tensor of shape (1,2)

Return guidance on parameters & behavior notes:
- feint_amp and feint_freq control how provocative the feints are: increase for more luring but riskier behavior.
- release_threshold tunes patience; small maps or aggressive opponents may require smaller thresholds.
- The internal hold_counter allows short-lived, repeated feints and timed releases; it decays quickly when holding conditions do not persist.

Rationale and emergent team effects:
- By intentionally holding and feinting, this agent creates windows for teammate movement: defenders who commit to stopping the dribbler become out of position, enabling through passes or quick releases.
- The shielding point keeps the defender behind the ball-body line, increasing time to find teammate runs.
- When not appropriate to hold, the agent becomes a reliable inside outlet (not a wide decoy), balancing team shape.
- The defensive fallback prevents catastrophic exposure when our own goal is threatened.

Example returned action (implementation note): the pseudocode produces a 2D force vector 'force' which should be returned as torch.tensor([[force_x, force_y]]) clamped in magnitude to max_force (or max_force * burst during bursts).
